about.title: El Cajon Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Most people in El Cajon never think about who designed the tire on the family car until something goes wrong. When it does, California law puts the focus where it belongs: on the product, not on you. Under strict liability, an injured person generally has to show that an item was defective in its design, its manufacturing, or its warnings, and that the defect caused the harm. Proving the manufacturer was careless is usually not required. That distinction matters in a city of 103,679 residents in San Diego County, where public records logged 619 injury collisions and 891 people injured in 2025. Some of those crashes along I-8, Broadway, E Main Street and Fletcher Parkway may involve an airbag, brake, or tire that failed, and a product claim can run alongside the driver-fault questions. Whatever hurt you, keep it. Do not return it, repair it, or throw it out. LawProactive is not a law firm; we connect El Cajon residents, free of charge, with an independent attorney who handles defective product cases on contingency.

whyChoose.title: Why El Cajon Residents Turn to LawProactive for Defective Product Claims

items.title: Strict liability works in your favor
items.desc: In California you generally do not have to prove the manufacturer was negligent, only that the product had a design, manufacturing or warning defect that caused your injury. The attorneys we connect you with understand how to frame a claim around that standard.

items.title: We stress preserving the evidence
items.desc: The product itself is often the heart of the case, so we encourage you to hold onto it, along with packaging, receipts and photos. An attorney can arrange proper storage and expert inspection before anything is lost.

items.title: Every link in the chain gets examined
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors and retailers may all be liable under California law, even if the store in El Cajon simply sold the item. Identifying every responsible party can matter for a fair recovery, and our free connection service is designed to get that review started quickly.

items.question: My airbag did not deploy in a crash on I-8 near El Cajon. Could that be a product liability case?
items.answer: It might be. Traffic collisions on I-8, Broadway or Fletcher Parkway usually start as driver-fault claims, but if a safety component failed to work as designed, a separate claim against the vehicle or part manufacturer may exist. The car needs to be preserved and inspected before it is scrapped or sold, so speak with an attorney before authorizing repairs or a total-loss payout.

items.question: Do I have to prove the company was careless?
items.answer: Under California's strict liability rules, generally no. You typically need to show the product was defective in its design, manufacturing or warnings and that the defect caused your injury. This is different from most negligence cases, and it is one reason having an attorney who knows the standard can make the process more manageable.

items.question: I already threw the product away. Is my claim over?
items.answer: Not necessarily, though it does make things harder. Photos, receipts, medical records, the same model from a store, and recall notices can still help establish the defect. Contact LawProactive as soon as you can so an attorney can assess what evidence remains and what can still be gathered.
